Commentary.Commentary: That ends a terrific run chase from an ever-improving England side. Both teams have very less to lose when they meet each other in the final ODI at Cardiff on Saturday, 2nd July, 2016 at 1500 IST (0930 GMT). One will play for pride, Sri Lanka, while the hosts will aim to inflict more insult by winning the series 3-0. Do join us then. Adios! Take Care!

Man of the Match, JASON ROY says that it's an incredible win for the boys. He has put in lots of hard work, which is paying off now. He is glad to contribute to his team and will never forget his innings but is disappointed about how he got out. He says he will gladly accept the record for second highest ODI score by an English player. Comparing his two hundreds in the series, he says that both are different and special. While the first hundred was under control, they were under pressure to score in the second one. He credits the Sri Lankans with batting really well. He claims that while he is not be out of breath, his legs are feeling the pressure from running between the wickets. Repeats that he has great respect for the boys and that his hard work and graft is paying off. He is proud that he picked himself up from a low point in his career and of his contribution in this innings and series.

Victorious English captain, EOIN MORGAN says that it was a pretty special run chase. Praises Jason Roy for playing a match-winning innings and impressing all by making the most of his form. Praises the ground staff for preparing a superb wicket in spite of the rain in the last two days. Admits that his team was poor with the ball in the death overs and looks to improve in Cardiff. Feels that it is a short ground and restricting run-scoring is difficult. Wants to assess the plans ahead of the Cardiff ODI. Is impressed with his side's improved fielding today. Is very happy about his side overall and wants to play as much cricket as possible with this unit. Agrees that he was aware that Roy was approaching a record. Stresses that it is not about individuals but about wins.

Sri Lankan skipper, ANGELO MATHEWS admits that his team was not the best tonight. Praises Roy for his brilliant knock. Rues the injuries in the series. Is looking for a couple of changes in the next game.

It was not a day for the bowlers. Earlier in the day, England bowlers were sent all over the park and the hosts gave it back in some style. Everyone went for plenty and struggled to pick up wickets. Pradeep struck early but then the blows hardly came.

Moeen Ali came out to open today in place of the injured Alex Hales but could not last long. Roy then counter-attacked and Root took some momentum from him to get into form. Once Root fell, there was a slight chance for the Lankans but they needed the wicket of Roy. They could not get that and useful partnerships with Morgan and Bairstow for the opener sealed the chase. He finished with 162 from 118 balls, second highest score by an Englishman in ODIs, just 5 behind Robin Smith's 167.

It has all been about Jason Roy. He has single-handedly demolished the Lankan attack, scoring 52 percent of his team's runs. One would believe that he got an early reprieve by the umpire when he was on 16, regarding an LBW call but he played beautifully. He got good support from Root as the duo added 149 for the second wicket, which took the game away from the visitors.
WOW. That is some chase. 308 gunned down in 40.1 overs. Terrific batting. England have sealed the chase in excellent style, with a game to go.

NOT OUT. That is a bit debatable. Depends on what the individual is seeing at that point of time. In real speed, it was a full ball outside off, 73.7 mph, Roy came forward to defend but missed and was hit on the pads. Mathews and Chandimal appealed but the umpire shook his head. Both the keeper and bowler were convinced and Mathews went for the review. Now, if you actually look at Hawk Eye, it shows that the impact is outside off, which is fine. But looking at the shot played by Roy, it looked like the bat was behind the pad. So, he was not offering a stoke, isn't it? In that case, impact should not matter, correct?
